second_round_searches: OpenReview reviews, rebuttals and meta-reviews of the Harbor Adapters and Harbor-Index and the Terminal-Bench submissions (NeurIPS 2026 Datasets and Benchmarks track, ICLR 2026), searched for parity, overlap, SEM, standard error, equivalence, three-run and statistics terms, together with an OpenReview full-text search for 'parity experiment' and 'benchmark port' and a title screen of the accepted-paper lists of NeurIPS 2026 Datasets and Benchmarks, ASE 2026, ICSE 2027 cycle 1, ESEM 2026 and FSE 2026 (conf.researchr.org and dblp) for parity, port, harness, adapter, reproducibility, equivalence and Terminal-Bench.

Issue comments (since June 2025), pull-request comments and reviews of adapter pull requests in the harbor-framework harbor, adapters and terminal-bench repositories, searched for overlap, SEM, standard error, t-test, Welch, bootstrap, confidence interval, equivalence, TOST, power, underpowered, too few runs, noise, not sufficient and trivially; the commit messages of harbor and terminal-bench searched for parity, overlap and SEM; and every past version of the Harbor adapter-review script (src/harbor/cli/adapter_review.py) and workflow (.github/workflows/adapter-review.yml) checked for an earlier or proposed statistical check.

Monthly arXiv listings for September and October 2026 in cs.SE, cs.AI, cs.LG, cs.CL and stat.ML, screened by title for parity, port, harness, adapter, scaffold, migration, fidelity, equivalence, reproducibility, Terminal-Bench, Harbor and SWE-bench (abstract opened for every hit), plus Hugging Face Papers and alphaXiv searched for 'Harbor parity', 'benchmark port harness', 'equivalence test benchmark' and 'adapter fidelity', and Semantic Scholar searched for papers citing arXiv 2609.04298 and for 'Harbor parity adapter'.

All repositories of the harbor-framework and laude-institute GitHub organisations searched for 'parity' and 'original_runs'; the repositories, Harbor forks, branches, issues and pull requests of the Harbor adapter maintainers (crystalxyz, audreina17, kobe0938, Rebabit, Slimshilin, alexgshaw, mikemerrill) searched for parity, statistics, bootstrap, t-test and equivalence work; and arXiv and dblp searched for 2026 agent and benchmark papers by the Harbor paper's lead authors (Shaw, Merrill, Shi, Lin, Zhu, Zhou) and for 'Harbor adapters' and parity benchmark work.

Alternative vocabulary searched on the web, in OpenAlex and in GitHub issues ('adapter fidelity', 'harness drift', 'benchmark migration' fidelity, 'scaffold equivalence', 'faithful port', 'wrapped benchmark' or 'benchmark wrapper' validation, 'cross-harness' agreement or parity, 'harness-invariant' or 'harness-agnostic' scores, 'same benchmark, different harness' and 'port validation'), plus Chinese-language searches on Harbor adapter parity experiments and benchmark reproduction (web, Zhihu, Juejin, CSDN) and Japanese-language searches on Harbor adapter parity experiments and benchmark porting (Zenn, Qiita, note.com).

Crossref and OpenAlex records and forward citations (2023-2026, restricted to language-model, benchmark and leaderboard work) for Tukey (1959) 'A quick, compact, two-sample test to Duckworth's specifications' (Technometrics 1:31-48), Neave and Granger (1968) 'A Monte Carlo study comparing various two-sample tests for differences in mean', Schenker and Gentleman (2001) 'On judging the significance of differences by examining the overlap between confidence intervals', Payton, Greenstone and Schenker (2003), Cumming and Finch (2005) 'Inference by eye' and Belia et al. (2005), plus web searches for overlapping error bars or confidence intervals on LLM leaderboards and for Tukey's quick (pocket) test with three runs.

Tolerance rules for validating ports in other benchmark ecosystems: the MLPerf Inference and Training rules (99% of reference accuracy, equivalence to the reference implementation), the lighteval reference scores and their tolerance, the Hugging Face transformers model-porting tolerance (atol), the MLCommons AlgoPerf framework-parity tests between JAX and PyTorch, the Epoch AI Benchmarking Hub and Artificial Analysis methodologies on own results versus lab-reported scores, the OpenCompass, Evalchemy and lighteval tolerances for reproducing reported scores, the UK AISI Inspect blog on validating evals, METR task-port validation, and web searches for reference-implementation tolerance and accuracy-target equivalence rules.

Community and talk channels searched for Harbor parity, adapters and run counts: Discord archives indexed on answeroverflow.com and linen.dev, talks and transcripts by the Terminal-Bench and Harbor maintainers (Alex Shaw, Mike Merrill, the Laude Institute Terminal-Bench 2.0 launch) and the Latent Space, Cognitive Revolution and AI Engineer episodes on Terminal-Bench, X threads by Alex Shaw, Mike Merrill, Lin Shi and the Laude Institute, Reddit (r/MachineLearning, r/LocalLLaMA), the Hugging Face forum, the laude.org blog, LessWrong and Bluesky.
